content.content:
An X post carries no link, not even to his own blog, because X cuts the reach of a post that sends the reader off the platform and a Zernio post pays that toll unwatched. `pair_tweet.py` refuses a body with a URL in it. The Note keeps its link.

X threads are retired and so is the pinned first comment, which is a LinkedIn mechanic. Atharva is on X Premium+, so one post carries up to 25,000 characters and the reason to split one no longer exists.

## Start every session here, never with a file hunt

One command answers "where does the work stand and what do I do next". Run it before you ask him anything about the pipeline, and run it again when a piece ships.

```bash
python SCRIPTS/next.py
```

It reads the current season, the drafts behind each beat, the slop score of the next one, and the review desk. It prints one next action and the exact command that does it. `--all` prints every remaining beat in order. It writes nothing and it never fails loudly, so it is safe to run at any point in a session.

Requests such as "what should I write next", "where was I", "what is the status", "what is left" or "pick up where we left off" all mean this command. Run it and act on the answer rather than reading the season file, the drafts folder and the desk by hand.

## Writing rules, defined in one place only

**Start at `DIGITAL TWIN/core/runtime-contract.md`.** That file is the load order. It names which files always load, which one loads on demand, which channel skill owns the job, and which checks run at the end, in order. Five files always load: the contract, `DIGITAL TWIN/core/pattern-rules.md` (the failure shapes the scorer cannot see, plus the restraint rules that stop an edit sanding a draft flat), `DIGITAL TWIN/core/write-simply.md` (the plain style, and the test that a sentence reading badly means the idea under it is wrong), `DIGITAL TWIN/World.md`, and `DIGITAL TWIN/core/net-new-value.md`. A hook, `.claude/hooks/writing-load-order.py`, prints the chain into context on any writing prompt, and `SCRIPTS/loadorder/block.py` renders the load-order panel above the draft. That panel is rendered rather than typed, so its checks half reports what the scorers actually returned.

**Net New Value is the guiding principle for all content, on every channel.** `DIGITAL TWIN/core/net-new-value.md` holds the grid. Name the box of the core insight before you draft. Only box 4 ships: non-obvious to the reader and tactical enough to use today. The load-order panel carries an `insight` line for it.

`World.md` names the villain, the vision, the one reader and the skill tree, so it decides what a piece is for. Every draft names the skill-tree node it advances before the first line, and the load-order panel carries a `node` line with it. The current season is `SUBSTACK/GROWTH STRATEGY/Season 01 - The Owned System.md`. Never restate the villain or the vocabulary anywhere else, because a copy goes stale.

`DIGITAL TWIN/AI Writing Policy.md` is the central directive and it outranks everything in this section. Read it before any writing task. The files below say what to avoid, and that file says what the writing is for, so it decides the calls the rules do not cover.

1. Each prose rule is one file in `DIGITAL TWIN/rules/`, and its README explains the stages and the two profiles. `SCRIPTS/slop/slop_rules.py` holds the regex tables. Nothing else defines a writing rule.
2. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` carries the generated numbered copy that loads every session. Never hand-edit that block.
3. Run `python SCRIPTS/slop/score.py "<file>" --write` to check a file. CRIT must reach 0.
4. To change a rule, edit its file in `DIGITAL TWIN/rules/` (or `slop_rules.py` for a regex), then run `python SCRIPTS/slop/rules_prompt.py --write`. `--check` exits 1 on drift.
5. Never restate a rule here or in any other file. Link instead.

`DIGITAL TWIN/Voice.md` holds persona, which is a separate concern. `DIGITAL TWIN/Long-Form Writing Rules.md` holds long-form craft. Neither repeats a rule from `slop_rules.py`.

A channel skill carries the shape of its channel and nothing else. The ban lists live only in `slop_rules.py`.

### The pipeline blocks, it no longer reminds

`.claude/hooks/writing-gate.py` runs the scorers itself and refuses. # Story Data: How neatlogs and Entire Changed FirstRun

Read back on 2026-10-11 between 10:20 and 11:30 IST with `neatlogs-cli` 0.2.0 (OAuth user, project `e6bcef18-b18b-4745-90b1-3691c29c2493`), `entire` and `git`. Nothing in neatlogs or Entire was created, changed or deleted to make this file.

Every number carries a label. **Measured** means it was read from a neatlogs or Entire API, a span payload, `docs/runs/index.json` or git on 2026-10-11. **Inferred** means it joins two measured facts by time or by reasoning. **Claimed** means an earlier file in this repo states it and no API returns it.

Times are UTC unless marked IST. IST is UTC + 5:30.

## 1. Neatlogs Holds 205 Traces and $1.76 of Model Cost

**Trace count (measured, `traces list --from 2026-10-01`).** 205 traces in the project. The first is 2026-10-08 17:48, the last is 2026-10-10 19:29. No trace arrived after that, so nothing ran on 2026-10-11 before this read.

| Workflow | Trace name | Traces | Trace status ERROR | Cost in traces |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| firstrun | firstrun.run | 67 | 50 | $1.5682 |
| firstrun | firstrun.audit | 34 | 0 | $0 (no model call) |
| firstrun | firstrun (bisect and early roots) | 6 | 1 | $0.0414 |
| firstrun | firstrun.prereqs | 3 | 3 | $0 |
| firstrun | firstrun.bisect | 2 | 2 | $0 |
| firstrun | claude_agent.query (orphan roots) | 2 | 0 | $0.1244 |
| firstrun | probe.a, probe.b, probe.c, firstrun.hello | 4 | 0 | $0 |
| neatlogs-app | junk test traces from pytest | 82 | 33 | $0.0214 |
| neatlogs.doctor.v2 | doctor.probe.root | 4 | 0 | $0 |
| support-bot | handle_request (not FirstRun) | 1 | 1 | $0 |

- Total cost in all traces: **$1.7553** (measured). `analytics cost --workflow firstrun` gives $1.7340 over 118 traces.
- Per day: 2 traces on 2026-10-08 (support-bot and 1 other), 203 on 2026-10-10 (measured).
- `analytics kpis --workflow firstrun`, 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-12: 119 traces, error rate 0.471, detection hit rate 0.454, average duration 172.8 s (measured).
- The 82 `neatlogs-app` traces came from a pytest fixture leak, fixed before 08:14 UTC on 2026-10-10. `traces delete` returns `NOT_FOUND_OR_OPERATION_DISABLED` with `operationGate: tier-c-compute`, so they stay (claimed in the friction log, gate not re-tested).

**Trace status is not the run result.** A failed `step.<id>` span rolls ERROR up to the trace even when the root span says `verified` (see `docs/neatlogs-integration.md`, "Open limits"). Use the root span output or `docs/runs/index.json` for outcomes, never the trace status.

**firstrun.run by tag (measured, cost and duration from the trace).**

| Tag | Runs | First to last (UTC) | Mean cost | p95 cost | Mean duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev | 7 | 07:35 to 08:44 | $0.0031 | $0.0169 | 78 s |
| v1 | 4 | 07:40 to 07:47 | $0.0262 | $0.0397 | 128 s |
| check | 4 | 08:10 to 08:18 | $0.0065 | $0.0211 | 108 s |
| v2 | 8 | 08:59 to 09:44 | $0.0333 | $0.1014 | 204 s |
| real | 12 | 08:59 to 10:42 | $0.0285 | $0.0508 | 446 s |

| real2 | 7 | 11:33 to 11:57 | $0.0404 | $0.0596 | 261 s |
| tiercap | 3 | 12:27 to 12:40 | $0.0032 | $0.0045 | 118 s |
| none | 1 | 14:37 | $0.0327 | | 138 s |
| radar | 18 | 17:21 to 17:46 | $0.0186 | $0.0512 | 200 s |
| radar-v2 | 2 | 17:38 to 17:48 | $0.0600 | $0.0653 | 410 s |

All 67 runs: mean $0.0234, p95 $0.0547, max $0.1014 (trace `a462576e751e91543b5623185331d603`, v2 OpenAI fixture). 17 runs cost more than $0.035.

Trace cost undercounts. LLM spans carry fresh input tokens only, so the run log (`docs/runs/index.json`) and `state.json` show higher figures. Example: dlthub trace `1b47ffa6` holds $0.0512, its run log row says $0.10.

**Tool spans (measured, `analytics tools`).** `step.1` ran 130 times with 46 errors, `step.2` 105 times with 36 errors, `step.3` 80 times with 21 errors. `classify_failure` ran 71 times with 0 errors. `read_docs` ran 60 times with 2 errors.

**Run outcomes from the root span (measured, `traces payload <trace> <root span> --fields output`, 66 of 67 runs read).** 28 failed, 22 verified, 9 passed, and 8 roots carry no status (the 4 v1 runs and 4 early dev and check runs predate the root output). By tag: v2 3 failed, 3 passed, 2 verified. real 6 failed, 6 verified. real2 3 failed, 4 verified. radar 8 failed, 6 verified, 4 passed. radar-v2 1 passed, 1 verified. tiercap 2 failed, 1 verified.

**False fails with exit code 0 (measured).** 11 `step.<id>` spans in 7 runs have status ERROR, `exit_code` 0 and `passed` false. The step ran, and only the expected-output or file check failed. They are dlthub `1b47ffa6` step 2 (2 spans), uv `57b8ba9f` step 3, uv `14e57f34` step 4, Dagster `b3b5dd14`, `08379c21` (2 spans) and `35f401fc`, and MkDocs `a73e1c42` (3 spans, fixed by `2de852f`).
